text:
The court should most likely apply Washington law and deny the punitive damages claim. Under Washington's most-significant-relationship test, Washington's strong public policy against punitive damages probably outweighs California's place-of-injury connection, as I recall *Dailey v. North Coast Life Insurance Co.* (Wash. 1996) holding, though I have not re-verified that case in this session. The main risk is that a court focused on California as the place of injury could apply California law and allow the claim.

CONFIDENCE: 55
